newsitem.title: UK: LucasVarity up after share buy-back, div cut.
newsitem.headline: LucasVarity up after share buy-back, div cut.

text.p: Shares in car components group LucasVarity Plc, merged last year, rose 4-1/2 pence to 205 after the company cut its dividend to 4.5 pence, but compensated with a three percent share buy-back.
The stock market had been keenly awaiting the dividend news amid confusion whether it would be held at seven pence or trimmed and combined with a buy-back.
The eventual cut in the dividend was less than some analysts had expected, helping LucasVarity shares, but uncertainties over the dividend policy remained, one industry watcher said.
But Lucas Varity quickly dispelled uncertainty by saying in an interview the group plans a continuing programme of dividend growth and share buy-backs.
"We expect to see the dividend increase each year in line with profits and continuing share buy-backs," chief executive Victor Rice said.
But some analysts were still sceptical about the prospect for dividend hikes.
"They alluded to difficult trading conditions, suggesting that operating profits and dividends are not going to storm ahead," one said.
LucasVarity also reported full-year proforma pre-tax profit of 282 million stg, meeting most analysts expectations.
But profits were of little importance as it did not include any savings from the LucasVarity merger. LucasVarity said earlier that merger synergies would operate only in 1998.
